From: Emma Li <emma@stratus.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing request: reserved GPU fleet for StratusAI inference

Hi Ben —

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: StratusAI is launching a multimodal assistant for enterprise docs (search + generation). We expect a mix of short retrieval-augmented prompts and longer single-turn generation for summaries. High-level forecast for the first 12 months:
- Avg daily active users: 85k
- Peak concurrent requests (p95): ~5.5k simultaneous in-flight requests
- Typical prompt length: 100–180 tokens
- Typical model response: 400–900 tokens (median ~520)
- Expected average requests per active user per day: 3 (spiky during business hours)

Our latency SLO is 450ms p95 for short prompts (<200 tokens) and 1.2s p95 for longer summarization calls. We will host sensitive customer data and need VPC + SOC2 evidence later.

Can you help us translate this into an initial reserved capacity recommendation and any questions you need filled out? I attached a small sample of traces and a token distribution CSV.

Thanks —
Emma Li
Head of Platform
StratusAI

Attachment: stratus_token_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet with token_length,count,time_bucket)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@stratus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: reserved GPU fleet for StratusAI inference

Emma —

Appreciate the context and the token profile. Quick clarifying questions so we can give a tighter reserved-capacity plan:

1) Are your 5.5k p95 concurrent requests distributed evenly across an 8–10 hour business day window or concentrated into shorter burst windows?
2) How many of those requests require retrieval (RAG) vs. pure generation? RAG adds CPU/embedding cost and potential extra calls to the model for re-ranking.
3) Do you have a target model family in mind (open Llama-family variant, LLM-Redwood-v1, or something else)? Quantization/precision (fp16 vs 4-bit) matters a lot for sizing.
4) Are you okay with graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model family) during very large spikes?

I routed this to Marissa (solutions) — she'll send a short questionnaire we use for fleet sizing and an initial estimation template. If you prefer, we can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through it.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the sample. To produce an explicit reserved-fleet recommendation I need a few specifics. I pasted the compact questionnaire below so you can reply inline — this helps us turn data into GPU-hours, model choices, and expected latency headroom.

Questionnaire (please reply inline):
1) Traffic shape: what fraction of daily traffic falls into the top 2 hours of the day? (e.g., 40%)
2) Burst factor: when you say \"peak concurrent 5.5k\" — is that sustained for minutes or seconds? Typical duration?
3) Session vs stateless: do you maintain multi-step sessions with KV cache per session (and average session length in turns)?
4) Retrieval mix: percent of requests that include a RAG pipeline (retrieve -> embed -> rank -> generate)
5) Acceptable quantization: can you accept 4-bit for base models or must we use fp16 for highest quality?
6) Latency target breakdown: p50/p95 for <200 tokens and >=200 tokens; are p99 targets strict?
7) Autoscaling: do you want reserved only, or reserved + burst (reserved + transient on-demand capacity)? Preferred burst cap?
8) Disaster recovery: required RTO/RPO and cross-region failover needs?
9) Privacy/Isolation: any must-have on-disk encryption or HSM/KMS requirements beyond standard SOC2?
10) Any existing throughput tests (QPS traces) or a synthetic traffic generator we can run?

Attachment: stratus_workload_samples.json (sample request traces, anonymized)

If helpful, Vivek can sketch an initial mapping (e.g., X H100s or Y A100s) once we have answers to 1–5 and traffic shape.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Emma Li <emma@stratus.ai>

Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2029 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: reserved GPU fleet for StratusAI inference — short questionnaire

Marissa —

Answers inline below. Attaching an anonymized 3-day trace and a small summary CSV.

1) Traffic shape: ~55% of daily volume falls into the 3-hour morning peak (US/EU overlap).
2) Burst factor: Peaks can sustain ~6–10 minutes during market open windows; short spikes (seconds) up to 2x above that occasionally.
3) Session vs stateless: Mostly stateless calls, ~18% are multi-turn sessions with average 3.2 turns; KV cache not required initially, but may be in v2.
4) Retrieval mix: ~42% of requests trigger RAG (embedding + retrieve + rerank) before generation.
5) Acceptable quantization: We prefer fp16 for top-level generation quality for launch, but willing to test 4-bit for non-critical paths.
6) Latency targets: short calls (<200 tokens) p95 <= 450ms, p99 <= 800ms; long calls (>=200 tokens) p95 <= 1.2s, p99 <= 2.5s.
7) Autoscaling: We want reserved + burst; reserved baseline for predictable SLAs and a burst cap of +40% capacity on-demand.
8) DR: cross-region failover desirable with RTO <= 15m for critical endpoints.
9) Privacy: KMS integration required, disk encryption at rest + audit log retention 12 months.
10) Tests: attached 3-day traces and a small synthetic qps generator we can run together.

Attachments: stratus_workload_samples.json, stratus_token_profile.xlsx

Thanks —
Emma

Subject: RE: Reserved fleet sizing — StratusAI discovery & next steps

Emma / Carlos —

Great — thanks for the fast turnaround and the traces. Based on the numbers you provided and the attached traces, here's a high-level initial recommendation to seed the reserved fleet and the immediate next steps: 

Initial reserved footprint (launch baseline):
- Model assumption: fp16 large decoder-only (Redwood-compat bfloat/fp16) with evaluation plan to pilot 4-bit for non-critical routing
- Baseline reserved GPUs: 6x H100-80GB nodes (assuming ~900–1,100 effective concurrent short-prompt slots per H100 for your prompt/response mix).
- Burst/Autoscale: allow an additional +40% on-demand (up to 2–3 extra H100 equivalents) to handle 6–10 minute sustained peaks.
- RAG overlay: provision an additional 2x medium GPUs or CPU-backed embedding tier for retrieval/embedding processing to keep embedding latency separate from generation SLOs.

Rationale notes:
- With ~55% of traffic in a 3-hour peak and p95 targets under 450ms, the reserved baseline prioritizes p95 latency headroom while minimizing token cost.
- RAG percent (~42%) means we separate retrieval to avoid degrading generation slots; embeddings are CPU-friendly but we recommend dedicated mid-sized GPU nodes if you do dense vector search at high QPS.
- If we safely adopt 4-bit on 20–30% of requests, we can defer ~1 H100-equivalent of capacity to reduce cost; we'll validate with quality A/B tests.

Next steps / action items:
1) Ben: schedule an ops call with your infra (30 min) to run the synthetic load generator against a Redwood test cluster — propose Thu 13 Jun 09:00 PT.
2) Marissa & Vivek: prepare a short sizing workbook (mapping qps->GPU-hours) and a suggested pilot plan (2-week canary with gradual ramp).
3) Emma: confirm cross-region DR priority and provide initial list of sensitive customers that need HSM/KMS isolation for compliance.
4) Laura: share SOC2 evidence pack and our private deployment checklist during procurement.

I'll iterate the detailed reserved-capacity quote after the synthetic run and we can convert to a committed reserved contract (monthly billing) once traffic patterns are validated.

Best,
Ben Carter
